```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"

```

MSstatsConvert does not provide a converter for AlphaPept. This vignette shows
the recommended workflow for such a tool: a language model proposes the
mapping to the MSstats format, the user checks it, and MSstatsConvert converts
the data for the analysis with MSstats. The mapping was obtained once and
saved, so the vignette runs without a language model, an API key or a network
connection.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(MSstatsConvertLLM)
library(data.table)
```

# The export

We use the AlphaPept output of the ProteoBench benchmark for label-free
DDA, a subset of the three-species mixture of Van Puyvelde et al.
(2022). Human, yeast and *E. coli* proteins are mixed in two proportions,
conditions A and B, with three runs each. The source, the license and the
design of the file are described in `inst/extdata/README`.

```{r export}
input <- fread(system.file("extdata", "AlphaPept_subset.csv",
                           package = "MSstatsConvertLLM"))
annotation <- fread(system.file("extdata", "AlphaPept_annotation.csv",
                                package = "MSstatsConvertLLM"))
str(input)
annotation
```

# Inferring the mapping

`infer_mapping()` sends the column names and three example rows of the export
to the model, and returns the mapping that the model proposes. We obtained the
saved mapping with the call below, using deepseek-r1-14b and the filter-aware
prompt, after one discarded call. The script
`inst/scripts/make_new_format_mapping.R` repeats it.

```{r infer-live, eval = FALSE}
mapping <- infer_mapping(input, "deepseek-r1-14b", "filter_aware",
                         acquisition = "DDA")
```

Here, we read the saved mapping instead.

```{r infer-saved}
path <- system.file("extdata", "new_format_mapping.rds",
                    package = "MSstatsConvertLLM")
if (!nzchar(path)) {
  stop("The saved mapping inst/extdata/new_format_mapping.rds is missing. ",
       "Build it with Ollama running and deepseek-r1-14b pulled:\n",
       "  Rscript inst/scripts/make_new_format_mapping.R\n",
       "then reinstall the package.", call. = FALSE)
}
mapping <- readRDS(path)
```

# The proposed mapping

The mapping gives, for each MSstats field, the column that the model chose and
its confidence. The export has no fragment ion, product charge or Q-value
column, so the model left these fields empty, with a confidence of zero.

```{r mapping}
proposed <- as.data.frame(mapping$mappings)
proposed[, c("field", "from", "confidence")]
```

# Checking the mapping

Before converting, check three choices, in this order: the intensity column,
the peptide sequence and the filters. The intensity must be
a quantitative column of the export, here `ms1_int_sum_apex_dn`. The peptide
sequence must be the modified sequence `sequence` rather than the stripped
sequence `sequence_naked`, since otherwise the modified and unmodified forms
of a peptide are merged into one feature. The two columns differ on the rows
shown below.

```{r check-fields}
chosen <- setNames(proposed$from, proposed$field)
numeric_columns <- names(input)[vapply(input, is.numeric, TRUE)]

c(intensity = chosen[["Intensity"]], peptide = chosen[["PeptideSequence"]])
numeric_columns
head(unique(input[sequence != sequence_naked, .(sequence_naked, sequence)]), 3)
```

The model proposed one filter, which keeps the rows that are not decoys.

```{r check-filters}
if (NROW(mapping$filters) > 0) {
  as.data.frame(mapping$filters)[, c("column", "operation", "value")]
} else {
  "no filters proposed"
}
```

The decoy filter is applied by default. It sets the intensities of the decoy
matches to missing, and since a decoy feature is then missing in every run,
MSstats drops it. To keep the decoys, for example to inspect them, drop the
filter from the mapping. Decoy features are usually measured in few runs, so
the conversion must also keep features with few measurements.

```{r keep-decoys}
with_decoys <- mapping
with_decoys$filters <- subset(as.data.frame(mapping$filters), column != "decoy")
NROW(with_decoys$filters)
```

```{r keep-decoys-convert, eval = FALSE}
converted_with_decoys <- LLMtoMSstatsFormat(input = input, annotation = annotation,
                                            llm_mapping = with_decoys,
                                            removeFewMeasurements = FALSE,
                                            use_log_file = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
```

# Changing a field by hand

The mapping is a data frame, so you can change any field before converting.
Here the model already chose the modified sequence, so the line below changes
nothing, but it shows how to correct the field if the model had chosen the
stripped sequence.

```{r fix}
mapping$mappings$from[mapping$mappings$field == "PeptideSequence"] <- "sequence"
mapping$mappings[mapping$mappings$field == "PeptideSequence", c("field", "from")]
```

# Validating the mapping

`validate_mapping()` checks the mapping itself, for example that no column is
assigned to two fields and that no required field is missing.

```{r validate}
validation <- validate_mapping(mapping)
validation$passed
validation$issues
```

# Saving the checked mapping

We recommend saving the checked mapping and publishing it with the analysis.
It records how the data were converted, even after the model changes.

```{r save-mapping}
mapping_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "AlphaPept_mapping.json")
jsonlite::write_json(mapping, mapping_file, auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE)
file.exists(mapping_file)
```

# Converting

`LLMtoMSstatsFormat()` applies the mapping and the annotation, and runs the
same processing steps as the hand-written converters of MSstatsConvert.

```{r convert, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
converted <- LLMtoMSstatsFormat(input = input, annotation = annotation,
                                llm_mapping = mapping,
                                use_log_file = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
head(converted, 3)
```

The `diagnostics` attribute lists the proposed filters that were applied and
those that were skipped, and any column named in the mapping that does not
exist in the export.

```{r diagnostics}
diagnostics <- attr(converted, "diagnostics")
diagnostics$applied_filters
diagnostics$skipped_filters
diagnostics$hallucinated_columns
```

# Differential abundance analysis

The converted table is in the MSstats format, so `dataProcess()` and
`groupComparison()` take it without further changes.

```{r dataprocess, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, results = "hide"}
processed <- MSstats::dataProcess(converted, use_log_file = FALSE)
contrast <- matrix(c(-1, 1), nrow = 1,
                   dimnames = list("B-A", c("A", "B")))
compared <- MSstats::groupComparison(contrast, processed, use_log_file = FALSE)
```

```{r results}
head(compared$ComparisonResult[, c("Protein", "log2FC", "adj.pvalue")], 3)
```

Since the species are mixed in known proportions, the expected log2 fold
changes of condition B against condition A are 0 for human, -1 for yeast and
+2 for *E. coli*. The median fold changes estimated from the converted table
are close to these values.

```{r species}
result <- as.data.table(compared$ComparisonResult)
result[, species := fcase(grepl("_HUMAN", Protein), "HUMAN",
                          grepl("_YEAST", Protein), "YEAST",
                          grepl("_ECOLI", Protein), "ECOLI",
                          default = "other")]
result[!is.na(log2FC), .(proteins = .N, median_log2FC = round(median(log2FC), 2)),
       by = species][order(species)]
```
